Crop to shape

A new Enhance row, and the preview it opens. Card, list and key row are captured from the app as it is today at 80 × 24; switch dark and light at the right of the tab bar. The photo is a drawn test scene.

★ 1 · The preview2 · The row3 · Wider than the photo4 · Zoom

After ↵ on Crop to shape ‹ 1:1 ›, a screen shows where the crop falls, before Save as. It opens where Sharp’s attention strategy puts it (on this photo it found the person: left 1,008 px), and ←→ moves it one step — 1/32 of the width. At its largest a crop spans the whole width or the whole height, so one pair of arrows moves it; + − zoom (tab 4) frees all four. The picture is half-blocks, so it works in every terminal and moves instantly. Once the crop has moved, r reset joins the key row and puts it back on the guess. Each figure: at the guess, moved four steps left, at the left edge.

Crop to shape is one row after Resize, in the built-in group. Highlighted, it gets Boost’s pill at the band’s far end: ←→ steps 1:1 · 4:5 · 16:9 · 9:16, the arrow grey where there is no step. The pane says what the shape becomes. A shape the photo already has is left out of the pill.

16:9 is wider than this 4:3 photo, so the crop spans the whole width and ↑↓ moves it instead; the key row says so. Drawn in P3.

+ zooms in: the crop gets smaller around its own centre, 10 % of the largest crop a step, down to 20 %. − zooms back out to the largest. Zoomed in, the crop no longer spans a whole side, so all four arrows move it. The second line says how much of the photo is kept. r undoes zoom and moves together, back to the guess. Drawn in P3.
